newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela labor law reforms go to Congress Monday.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela labor law reforms go to Congress Monday.

text.p: Venezuela's Congress will begin discussion next Monday of a package of labor reforms, part of the ground-breaking agreement reached late last month between unions, business and government, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said.
Despite the reforms' complexity -- some 20 articles in the Labor Law have to be changed -- Congress's "general mood looks to be to approve it," Petkoff said in an interview Thursday on Union Radio.
"Moreover, the faster it (the bill) is passed, the faster the new minimum salary will be established," Petkoff added.
Under a Tripartite agreement signed March 17, President Caldera must announce a new minimum wage once the bill is passed.

The bill prescribes far-reaching changes in Venezuela's onerous severance pay system, as well as wider reforms in the country's crumbling social security system including the setting up of private pension funds.
"We want to re-make the Social Security Law, but it won't be as fast as the reform of the Labor Law," Petkoff said.
